utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. I take it that the parties have received an electronic version of the list by the witness, although I think it is only the Word format part of what was presented earlier. And, of course, it's in B/C/S, but names are easy to compare. Mr. Lukic, no news about other versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No news, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pavlovic. Before we continue --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind that you you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. MacDonald will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There was one thing I should address to the Bench. I do plan to ask Mr. Pavlovic some questions about the new list, and in that regard, I would ask for some extra time to be given for cross-examination, between half an hour and an hour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't have prepared for this before you had received it, so to the extent necessary, Mr. Lukic, I thought that the list was just shorter, but -- but I leave at this moment in your hands, but we'll follow closely the type of questions you will put to the witness in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'm going to begin by asking you some questions about the two lists of individuals that we now have. Just to avoid any confusion, the list that the Defence was asking you about, the list that we were discussing yesterday, I'm going to call that the old list; and the list that we received yesterday, I'm going to call that the new list. We can agree to do that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The old list, that list had a title, Mr. Pavlovic. Who gave it that title?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave an overview of the cases, and I suppose that they were sent for translation, and we probably gave the title together or I probably said how it could be called, but I cannot remember the details right now. I can just repeat that I worked under conditions that were far from normal. We were doing many things simultaneously and it's impossible for me to remember every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, it's a straightforward question, Mr. Pavlovic. Who gave it the title? Did you give it the title? Did Mr. Lukic and the Defence give it the title, who wrote the title?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, no. The question can be -- Mr. MacDonald can insist on a clear answer on his question. Could you tell us who gave the title? You? The Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can just repeat that I do not remember due to the circumstances under which we had to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's a clear answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it's in your report. Is that not so, sir? It's part of your report, this list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the list was included in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you are the author of the report and the list -- and the list as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am the author of the report and the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, just to make sure we're speaking about the same thing when you answered His Honour Judge Moloto's question, are you saying that this list, the list of individuals, the overview, was a part of the report you submitted in June 2013?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a difficult question because I didn't know whether I would be testifying or not up until one and a half days before I was supposed to leave in order to travel here. I sent the materials in June, if you say that it was at that point in time, probably it was. And when I was told that I would be testifying, that I would be a witness, I then brought with me a group of statements and the list that was to be completed, the one that we talked about yesterday, the one that you're talking about now. Because I didn't know whether I would be testifying in the first place or not. The Defence didn't know that, and I could not consult them about the direction we would be moving in. That's why I'm talking about the conditions under which I had to work as a Defence expert witness from the very beginning and which were not normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Pavlovic, in response to His Honour Judge Moloto's question you said: "Yes, the list was included in my report." That list does not appear and is not referenced anywhere in the report you submitted in June 2013, does it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is mentioned are the arguments or, rather, the cases of possible - how would I call that? - omissions in the lists of missing persons. I only enclosed those specific cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, let me ask you this again and I'll clarify further. Firstly, the list that we spoke about yesterday, that does not appear in the report, it's not referenced in the report, and there are no names of individuals who had died in the report from that list. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the analysis itself, or the report, as you call it, if that's it, I'm talking about the analysis that I prepared, it's a material of 50 to 60 pages, does not contain names. It only mentions possibilities, things that may have happened, and then the list is an attachment to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, yes, the report does not contain any names. And this list is a list of names, and you say it's an attachment but it wasn't attached to it in June 2013, was it? In fact, the first time anybody was aware of this list was when you came here in The Hague in December?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. The first time the Defence, the Chamber, the Prosecution was aware of this list is when you arrived December. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I do not dispute that I brought that with me when I came here in December, but the reasons why that was so are that I didn't know whether I would testify or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no information whether I would be a witness here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, no one blames you for anything. If you just answer the questions, that's good enough. We're not saying it's right or wrong. We're just asking - at least Mr. MacDonald is - what happened. And Mr. MacDonald asked you whether, when you presented the report in June, whether the list was attached or known to the Defence, yes or no. Now you say, Well, it's not wrong -- no one says it's wrong. We just want to know. That's all. So, therefore, could you now please focus on the questions and answer them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I just want to clear this up, Mr. Pavlovic. When His Honour Judge Moloto asked you if it was part of your report and you said you included it, what I'm saying to you is that your report in June 2013 contains no names of people who died, contains no reference to this list, and does not incorporate this list that you brought with you in December. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question in the meantime, Mr. MacDonald. I'm sorry for that. Mr. Pavlovic, at the beginning of this discussion or question and answers, you said: "I gave an overview of the cases and I suppose that they were sent for translation and we probably gave the title together, or I probably said how it could be called ..." When you say "we probably gave the title together," who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say "we," I suppose that I told Mr. Branko Lukic what to write when he was supposed to sent it for translation. I suppose so because we worked under conditions that were not normal so I cannot claim with much certainty what exactly happened. As I told you, I was invited --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- just a few days before my testimony. Please allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. I asked you who is "we"? Just give the name. Who is "we"? Don't explain the whole procedure. I'm not interested in that. Who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I've just explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No. Please repeat. It was very unclear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that I suppose, it means that I cannot claim, I cannot assert, because we worked under conditions that were not normal, whether I told Mr. Lukic before he sent it for translation how to formulate the title. That's why I said "we."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, no. You are not answering my question. I would invite you to clearly state to whom you are referring when you are saying "we." Which persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I tried to tell you when I said "we," I had in mind the situation in which before the document was sent to be translated, I told Mr. Lukic what to write there. That's why I said "we." I'm repeating for the third time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you shouldn't repeat what I didn't want to hear. That means you are referring to Mr. Lukic and you. This is "we." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, you didn't say that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like it turn to the substance of the new list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And we uploaded that under 65 ter 33644, and that's not to be broadcast. If we could have that on the screen, please. We only have it in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it make any sense to have the old list and the new list together on the screen? I don't know whether you want to do any comparative thing. But if we only have the B/C/S, then at least we can compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I do plan to refer back to the old list, but I think I can guide the Court to it without requiring it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, as this comes up, if I can just ask you another question. At transcript page T42991 yesterday, I pointed out a duplicate in the old list to you, and you told the Court: "It is one more proof that this is a working version of the material." Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we look at page 1 in the list and it's the second name from the bottom, you see the name Salko Hrnjic, Mehmed, 1961. And if we can now turn to page 3 in the list, please, and we're looking about midway down, and there - yeah, that's fine - there we again see the name Salko Hrnjic, Mehmed, 1961. So this duplication, it's still on your new list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that. There's nothing I can say except that it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I just want to double-check, Mr. Pavlovic. There's not any other list, is there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the new list; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pavlovic, this is the new list. There isn't a newer list, a more final list, is there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we get into concrete examples, yesterday I read you a portion of your testimony where you said in response to question from His Honour Judge Orie that you exclusively chose examples where the eye-witness saw them die. And I read that out to you when we were talking about Azem Pasalic, and at transcript page 42956 going to 42960, you said: "Yes, I said that then, but after seeing this list, including cases that shouldn't be there, I cannot rule out the possibility that a working version of the list did not exclude the cases where there are witness reports saying that they had seen somebody die. Such cases should be excluded, and I see that the list is not the one I was thinking I was commenting on." So I'm right in saying that this final list that we have on the screen in front of us shouldn't have any examples where a person did not see someone die. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I understood the context of the statement, it shouldn't be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can go back to page -- no, sorry, we're on page 3 in the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You see the name Salko Hrnjic. The name above it is Muhamed Mehmedovic. We dealt with these two people yesterday, but in the interests of time I didn't show you the statement, the statement of Zijad Cikaric, but I'd like to show it to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 1D06273 on the screen, please. Your Honours, this is the statement the Defence uploaded, but in discussion with my colleague Ms. Stewart, we couldn't -- there was no English translation uploaded, but we found then an English translation so we uploaded the same statement with English translation, and that is 65 ter 33629. So my apologies. If we could turn to that one instead. And if we can have page 2 in both languages, please. Now, this is a long piece of text, but it's about halfway down in both languages. And we're looking for the two names, Salko Hrnjic, Muhamed Mehmedovic. In the English, it towards the bottom, just where the pointer was actually. In the B/C/S, it's more in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, what this witness says is that he saw four decomposing bodies at Snagovo and that he knew two of them, and he names Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic. And that is the first reference to these people's names in that statement, so far as I could see. So this is an example of somebody who clearly didn't see them die because he came across their decomposing bodies; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The witness says here the four who died at Snagovo, that is to say, Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic, both from Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Witness, could I ask you, even that's not what the statement says. The statement doesn't say that they died there, but the witness says that he saw four decomposed bodies and he talks about the dead he saw in Snagovo. That's not the same as seeing someone dying. It's -- it's different and, therefore, you're evading the question. Does this witness say, according to you, that he saw these persons dying; or did he say that he saw four decomposed bodies? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, please. Please allow me to explain. I will rather read directly what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I first want an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's just what I am offering, an answer, if you will allow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Which of the two" was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The second time when I was moving, two young men were killed in an ambush at Krizevacke Njive. The four who died at Krizevacke Njive I didn't know personally, but I knew two of the dead at Snagovo." Yes, yes, yes. Yes, this is actually another group of the four he saw at Snagovo who were decomposing and he recognised two, and he says there, as I already said: "I do not know the four who died at Krizevacke Njive, but I knew two of the dead at Snagovo. Those were Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic." Yes, he saw them dead here. He didn't see them die. But it was the combat zone, the zone of combat operations, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you to interpret. And would you next time before you answer a question, if it takes you so much time what it really says, do it preferably before you give your first answer so that we can save the time in getting this second answer now after you have read carefully the statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you were just saying that this person only saw them dead there, and then you were talking about the zone of combat operations and you say "so" -- what were you going to say there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the zone of combat operations but, in fact, I meant the line of breakthrough of this column, surrounded by the zone of combat operations. The fact that he saw these people dead entails an assumption that they died in combat. It cannot be proven unless by forensic investigation, but he saw them dead there, and I think the assumption is they died in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just check again whether there's any wrong translation. Did he see them die there or did he see them dead there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He saw them dead in an area where there was combat, where other people died in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you say so a second ago? Did you say "he saw them dead there," or did you say "he saw them die there"? Because then there may be a translation issue, and we always are very cautious in avoiding them, and we could have a correction to your words if you did not say "he saw them die there."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said others died in combat there, and he saw them dead. Not die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will be verified. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So, Mr. Pavlovic, when you come across a witness statement where somebody sees someone dead and the line of the breakthrough surrounded by a combat zone, you said the assumption is that they died in combat. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this specific case, yes. The assumption is they could have died during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I don't know if you have forgotten this, but yesterday when we spoke about these two victims, we went into private session and I read you the testimony of a witness. And it was very clear from that witness's testimony that these two people had been captured by the VRS and were the victims of summary execution. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I'm telling you that I made certain inferences based on this statement, an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And in this case, in this specific case, your assumption or inference that these people died in combat, that was wrong, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assumption that there is a possibility they could have died in combat, is it wrong? If I understood well, the statement that we looked at yesterday, if I remember well, that's also evidence that -- I can't remember the details. I can't say it's 100 per cent wrong, whether the investigation concerning specific persons has been finalized, I don't know. If -- if it has been finalized, I'm not disputing it. We have one witness on one side, and another witness on the other side. If the forensic investigation and the pathological investigation and everything has been finalized, then I'm not disputing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, there's one more question, Your Honours, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: -- it's not to do with the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, yesterday after I read that you information that was in transcript form, and you told the Court you'd only looked at statements, not transcripts, are you aware that that person also gave a statement in which he gave the same information and mentioned the same two names that are here on your list and that was disclosed to the Defence, it would have been among the material you would have reviewed. So you simply missed that statement of this person saying broadly the same thing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I told you yesterday that in searching the database, I focused on witness statements because transcripts are very long, 150 to 200 pages, and in such a short time I was not able to deal with that volume of material. I focused on statements given to security organs. Did I look at some transcripts? At some, probably, yes. But I concentrated on the breakthrough and the circumstances surrounding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Pavlovic. I just want to make sure that you've understood my question. What I'm saying to you is, the information in that transcript that I read to you yesterday is also contained in a witness statement. I'm asking you if you simply missed that information in your review of witness statements.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking through the statements, if I had noticed that that same person had been captured, I would probably have excluded that person from the list, but I didn't register it. I didn't notice it. There were many names of both witnesses and victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me alone, it's difficult to cover such a range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, the simple question was whether you missed it, yes or no, not whether you are to be blamed for missing it, but just Mr. MacDonald wants to know whether you missed it. And after a long answer you say: Well, more or less, if I would not have missed it then I would have seen, but there were a lot of names. That's all -- you missed it apparently. Otherwise you would have found it. You would have used it. Okay. So the simple answer to the question is: I must have missed it. That's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm just go to look at one more example on this list, Mr. Pavlovic. I don't think we need to look at any beyond that. Now, yesterday we looked at another victim, Ragib Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And if we have the new list on screen, 65 ter 33644, not to be broadcast. I'm looking at page 2 on the list. I think it's just in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, there with Ragib Mehmedovic, he is the fourth one up from the bottom, you're still referencing the witness statement of Seval Ademovic. And I'd like to look briefly at what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if we can have Seval Ademovic's statement on the screen, it's 1D06277, and page 3 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we briefly move into private session, Mr. -- Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber is satisfied that you were right, Mr. MacDonald. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, if we could have the witness statement of Seval Ademovic on the screen, page 3 in both languages. It's 1D06277.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: The second-last paragraph, I read this out to you yesterday, Mr. Pavlovic. All Seval Ademovic says is that: "I would like to point out that the following died in the breakthrough towards Tuzla," and the second name on the list, Ragib Mehmedovic. So this is another statement on your new list where the person making an identification doesn't explicitly say that he saw the victim die, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He doesn't say explicitly. It's not written here that he saw it, but if you know how witness statements are taken, and you know it, the questions are usually posed in the form of which of the persons do you know. And he says: "I stress that in the breakthrough to Tuzla, the following died ..." And he is speaking to an official security organ, be it military or public. So he knows it, the assumption is that he had seen it. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So when you see this phrase "died in the breakthrough," you assume that the person had seen the person die. I find that interesting, Mr. Pavlovic, because another person, another victim, on the old list that you cited to was Mujo Turkovic and for Mujo Turkovic, you also cited the witness statement of Seval Ademovic. So clearly you've read through the witness statement of Seval Ademovic, and you decided that Mujo Turkovic should come off of the new list and he is not there, but you decided that Ragib Mehmedovic should remain on the new list even although the same witness says exactly the same thing about both of them. Is that what you decided when you read the witness statement of Seval Ademovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, what you need to know about the way I proceeded in gathering this information and why I included someone, whether I was able to find them in the database of the missing or the dead, I need to know who that person is. Because the name itself doesn't mean anything to me if I'm not able to find that person on the list of the missing and identify it. It's possible that I was not able to find the second person and that's why I didn't include him. I can't remember the specific reasons. I found certain persons in certain witness statements, but I couldn't find out who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That's a long answer about how you proceeded in gathering information. What I'm asking you is that on Sunday, 13th of December, the day before you were due to testify, you had saved a version of this list which had Mujo Turkovic and Ragib Mehmedovic on it. For both of them, you cited to the witness statement of Seval Ademovic. And in this new list that you say is your final list, one of them is still there, one of them has been removed, even although Seval Ademovic says exactly the same thing about both of them. This is another mistake you've made, Mr. Pavlovic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would it be a mistake? I included one person. I didn't include the other. What the reasons are for not including someone, I would have to look at it again to tell you the reasons. And I stress to you once again in what conditions I was working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday during your testimony we dealt extensively with Mr. Turkovic. You explained to us that now having had a look at this statement of Seval Ademovic, that it was wrong to have him on that list. On today's list, we do not find Mr. Turkovic any further. Now, what Mr. MacDonald is asking you, whereas Mr. Mehmedovic was on the old list and is on the new list, why didn't you remove him? Because the basis for your doubts are found in the same statement in exactly the same wording. So why do you take out one from your old list and do not adopt him in your new list, and why the other one - for which the information is exactly the same - why does he remain on your list? And all your previous answers just are beyond what the gist of the question and the problem is. So when I earlier said whether you would please read before you give an impulsive answer, I now invite you also to think about the question and the gist of it and the problem which is addressed by Mr. MacDonald before you start giving long answers which are totally beyond the point. So, now, again, why, on the basis of exactly the same information, you took Mr. Turkovic off your list, he doesn't appear anymore; and why did Mr. Mehmedovic remain on the list although exactly the same information is, to your knowledge -- I see that you now start reading. Take your time, think about it, and then please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember why I did it at that moment. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: One last question on Ragib Mehmedovic. You may not remember this from yesterday, but we looked at another witness statement about Ragib Mehmedovic in private session. And Ragib Mehmedovic was last seen on a meadow with his hands on his head having surrendered. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So that I'm just going to summarise here what we've discussed. This new list, this final list which you produced, it still contains duplication. It still contains statements where the person didn't see the victim die. It still contains somebody last seen alive in the custody of the VRS on a meadow, and it still contains the names of people who were killed in summary executions. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statements that you've shown me, there are indications of that kind, yes, and I'm not disputing it. If you talk about people who ended up differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you've -- you have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Unless Your Honours have any further questions on the list, I would propose to move on to the report and it's here I thought I had about half an hour of cross-examination left, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please start.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, we're not going to discuss either list anymore. We're going to move to your report -- or I think you referred it to it as your analysis but we'll call it your report just to keep the terminology the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So if we can have MFI D01373 on the screen, please. And this can be broadcast, this is not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, the first 20 pages have been removed from your original report and I'm not going to look at the parts of the report where you talk about witness statements who see numbers of people dead. I'm just looking straight at the part where you talk about -- or things you cite to claim that there was some kind of clean-up of the battlefield. So if we can turn to page 31 in the English and page 28 in the B/C/S of your report. And what you do in this section, Mr. Pavlovic, is you cite one order of Ratko Mladic from the 20th of July, one order of the Drina Corps with regard to clearing up the battlefield. You say you couldn't find any reports that that took place. And then you go on to give two examples of what you claim is the clearing up of the battlefield taking place, and I'm just going to deal with those two examples. The first one is quite straightforward. If we can look for footnote 69 in the text. It's towards the bottom in the English, about midway in the B/C/S. You can look on the screen, Mr. Pavlovic. It's also there, or you can look in hard copy. Now, the text that this footnote purports to support is a claim by you that the roads in Zvornik municipality were being cleared up. And to support that, if we look down at footnote 69, it reads as follows: "While we were in Pobudje, we watched from a hill as the Chetniks were walking on the asphalt road in Pervani and collecting the dead bodies with a loader, which was then loading them into an," and if we turn the page in the English, "FAP truck. They were taking the bodies in the direction of the village of Kravica, Bratunac municipality." Mr. Pavlovic, where is Pervani village?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Pervani is between Kravica and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that, and we have maps to show that. The road going from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, that's in the Bratunac municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So the only reference you cite for roads in the Zvornik municipality being cleared is actually referring to something happening in the Bratunac municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain what was happening, and I cite an example what they were doing as far as roads are concerned. The roads had to be cleaned up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, all I'm asking is: In the main body of the text you specify the roads in the Zvornik municipality and the only thing you cite in the footnote is talking about something happening in the Bratunac municipality; that's correct, isn't it? That's all I'm asking just now.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite in the text that the roads, just after combat operations, had to be sanitized in order to become useable again. That's logical. And I cite one of the examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not claiming that this example applies to the Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we go back one page in the English, please, just to show the text again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, the line that you are purporting to support with this reference begins: "Similarly, the roads in Zvornik municipality where some of the fighting had taken place," and then you say, "also had to be cleared up soon after the cessation of combat operations." You are talking about the roads in the Zvornik municipality here. That's what this reference is for?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking in these two sentences about the roads in Bratunac municipality, citing a specific place, not about the Zvornik municipality. I'm talking about the roads that were used by the columns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Pavlovic. So I'm right in saying you have no reference here, no support for the idea that the roads anywhere other than the Bratunac municipality were cleared up? Just a yes or no to that one, sir. I think that's fairly clear, but can you confirm it for me?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not cite here any specific examples of sanitization of a road in the Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And, Mr. Pavlovic, are you aware that there's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm almost finished with this topic, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: There is already evidence related to the clearing up of bodies on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, and that, in fact, that evidence comes from one Prosecution fact witness - and that is RM306, Your Honours - and also pointed out in the report of the Prosecution investigator Dusan Janc in P01987. Are you aware that the Trial Chamber has already heard evidence about bodies being cleared up on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned here what I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So all you're aware of, then, in terms of evidence, is that there was some clearing up of the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. That's all that's in your report. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's all I mentioned, then that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am aware it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break. We'll take a break of 20 minutes, Witness. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. MacDonald, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: It was just to save time, Your Honours. If we could call up the exhibit I plan to ask the witness about. That is his report, D01373. Oh, it's still on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's still on our screen, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, I have one more item I'd like to discuss with you. You see on the screen there your report. Now, we dealt with the sentence before footnote 69. After footnote 69 -- it's on the screen, if you wish to look at that, Mr. Pavlovic. After footnote 69, you go on to cite a regular report dated 14th of July, 1995, from the engineering battalion based at Konjevic Polje. Now my first question here is: This report, that wasn't issued pursuant to the orders you cited just before it, was it? Do you need me to repeat the question, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this sentence only mentions that sanitization of the terrain was carried out, not that it was done in accordance with the above orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this report is dated 14th July 1995. I'm going to ask you if you're aware of some evidence in this case, Mr. Pavlovic, and perhaps you could just respond by saying either you are aware or you're not aware. Now, the evidence I would like to lay out for you is that on the 13th of July, 1995, a large number of the members of the column surrendered. They were held at Sandici meadow. And then just over a thousand of those people walked or were transported in buses to nearby Kravica warehouse, and then they were executed in Kravica warehouse on 13th July 1995 with guns and hand-grenades. Were you aware of that evidence, Mr. Pavlovic? And you can just say: I was aware or I was not aware.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not deal with this evidence and therefore I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Are you aware that Kravica warehouse is between 6 and 8 kilometres away from where the engineering unit who issued this report was based?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that the distance from Konjevic Polje to Kravica is what you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavlovic, I'd like to look at some other testimony about this document. Did you read any other person's testimony about what this document means?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I could see while working on this analysis from the materials --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I would just like to ask: Did you read any witness testimony about this document, about the report of the engineering battalion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about that specific document. I only know through Subotic's statement that some were taken prisoner and that some lost their lives during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to look at some -- what other people have said about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter number 1D01273.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And this is the testimony of General Milovanovic, whom I'm sure you were aware was the then-Chief of Staff of the VRS. We only have this in English so I'm going to read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'd like page 72 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Starting at line 14. This is his testimony in the Popovic case. In line 14: "Q. Okay. Let me read this to you. It says: "'A large enemy group was infiltrated in the region of Pobrdje Brdo and the region of Konjevic Polje. Units of the 5th Engineering Battalion and the MUP successfully resisted the enemy. About 1.000 to 1500 enemy civilians and soldiers were arrested and killed.' "Now, we talked about this before. Is there any justification to kill people after you arrest them?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I wonder if we can scroll down on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: "A. No, there isn't. It's a war crime." So the VRS Chief of Staff considers that this report is talking about a crime - in fact, a war crime. Now, my question for you, Mr. Pavlovic, General Milovanovic, the VRS Chief of Staff, he's going to have more experience than you in writing and reading military reports, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he has more experience in what you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And I'd like to move to the second person who talks about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can we have P03517. That is a public document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: As this comes up, Mr. Pavlovic, this is the testimony from a previous case, although it's evidence in this case, of Major Mile Simanic and he was the man who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: So in P03517, if we can have page 24 in the English. Again, this is only in English. And I'm looking to start at line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: "Q. Do you remember when I showed you this document in Bosnia, do you remember what you first said when you read that? "A. I said, 'God forbid,' or 'God Almighty,' or something like that. "Q. And why did you say that after reading this sentence? "A. Because at first I thought it was written meaning that the MUP and the Engineering unit did that."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now if we can turn over the page, please. And just underneath the black box at line 16, we have

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "The question was: 'Do you think, sir, what's described here in this document was a crime, no matter who did it?'" And at line 22, the witness answers: "In my view, whoever does something like that, it constitutes a crime."

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Again my question for you, Mr. Pavlovic: Major Mile Simanic, deputy commander of this unit, he is another person who has more military experience than you in terms of writing and reading military reports. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does. Though, as far as I know, he is not a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm going to look at one final bit of testimony with you, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we turn into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, we've seen one VRS officer, the one who wrote this report, say he thinks it's a crime. We've seen the VRS Chief of Staff, General Milovanovic, say he thinks it constitutes a war crime. And we have seen another person connected to these events say he is unaware of any other event it could be on that day. Mr. Pavlovic, this report, on the 14th of July, this report refers to the mass execution at Kravica warehouse on the 13th of July, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If Your Honours would bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: That concludes the cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacDonald. Mr. Lukic, any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pavlovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will start from the end because, as we've gone through these documents now, while they're still fresh in our minds, let's see. There was some talk about this document but only testimonies of several persons about this were shown to you, what they said about the document, and I will show you P03518. You have dealt with this document in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll just wait for the English translation to be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So Mile Simanic, a major, signed this document drawn up on the 14th of July, 1995. Let us read the sentence that other witnesses were questioned about in the given context. You were told that this could only refer to the killings at Kravica. Paragraph 1, enemy, reads as follows: "A large enemy group infiltrated in the Pobrdje Brdo region and the region of Konjevic Polje. Units of the 5th Engineering Battalion and the MUP successfully resisted the enemy." Let me ask you about this first part. On the 13th and the 14th of July, did you come across any information that combat was ongoing in the Pobrdje Brdo and Konjevic Polje areas?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Especially on the 13th. The 28th Division and the column were fighting while crossing the road between Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba. There were many casualties, and the sanitization of the terrain was under way. I believe that we already commented on this in the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we shall comment on the last sentence that the -- that was presented to the witnesses. We are not experts in semantics either of us, however, this sentence, is it properly written? Do you understand what it refers to: Arrested and killed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I viewed it in the context of the witness statements about events in this period, the 13th, because it refers to the 13th and possibly the 14th. What was going on in the area where the person who signed this document was at the time and also all the other statements that I had at my disposal. So in -- arrested and killed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a conjunction because it says "arrested, killed"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to what I learned from the statements about what was going on on the ground, I understood that this is just a confirmation of the information that many people were taken prisoner, as Mr. Subotic said, in Nova Kasaba at the stadium, and that the total number of people who were killed was between 1.000 and 1500. Once again, I repeat, because that was what the statements contained. That it refers to both categories, the arrested and the killed persons, that in total the number was between 1.000 and 1500, of both of these categories. Because he doesn't say that they were killed by firing squad but he says: Arrested, killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one short question. In the English translation of the document, we see "arrested and killed." And now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The translation is perfect in the sense the Prosecution asked, but it's not what the B/C/S version says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If there's any need to have "arrested and killed" being reviewed for the accuracy of the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours, this issue was litigated at great length in the Popovic case, in particular, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was not a Judge in the Popovic case and so, therefore, it's fine that you tell us. But apparently now "arrested, killed" comes up a few times now in the oral testimony, whereas the document says "were arrested and killed" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if there's anything you would like to -- I'm just raising the matter whether there's a -- and if you say it has been dealt with extensively in another case, then I think it's appropriate that the parties provide the Chamber with any information about what was at that time presented to the Popovic Chamber so that we are not making any mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The only point I was going to make was that in the B/C/S the Prosecution absolutely agrees it says "arrested, killed," but the translation has been vetted numerous times and that has been the translation put forward by CLSS. That was the only point I was going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So verification, Mr. Lukic, apart from whether it's right or wrong, but has the translation as it appears before us at this moment has been verified, if I understand Mr. MacDonald, again and again by CLSS and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's my mother tongue. I would never agree that's -- that means "arrested and killed" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, you don't have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It does not say that. Whoever claims it, it's not true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the only thing I wanted to establish whether this, right or wrong, that's for the Chamber later to consider, whether the translation as it appears before us on the screen, whether that has been verified thoroughly by CLSS although you do not agree with the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll check that. But we can ask Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Pavlovic is not someone who --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it -- in B/C/S does it say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- "arrested and killed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. MacDonald said it says "arrested, killed" and it is translated as it is now before us that has been verified. We don't need Mr. Pavlovic to verify any translation as made by CLSS. But I do understand that while observing "arrested, killed" and looking at the text, that it's -- it's an issue which apparently was dealt with extensively in the Popovic case, and I just want to avoid that there's any mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you yourself said that you and the witness are not experts in linguistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's true. But this much I can understand. I think. And I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- I ... we remain confident, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is not only semantics. It is whether there is "and" in the sentence or not. A simple question. There is no "and" in the sentence. There is no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we have understood that you disagree with the CLSS-verified translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today there has been much discussion of the criteria you applied for including something in your overview; that is to say, the table. It was stated that one ought to have seen somebody die in order to be able to testify whether somebody was indeed killed or not. Do you think and whether it was believed sufficient if someone saw a man dead and recognised him at a certain location but did not see the moment when the person died, was it considered sufficient in your work at the institute for missing persons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we collected information, information was very important for us so that we could establish the site where we might find the missing person, and, of course, we wanted to know something about the circumstances under which the person lost his or her life, if we were in a position to obtain such information at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then let us look again at a statement that had been put to you before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have one number and the Prosecution called it under another number. 65 ter 33629 is the one that I would like to call up because we have an English translation. That is the record of the statement of Zijad Cikaric. The date is 16 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A passage from the second page was put to you, so I'd like to see the second page in both versions. The last quarter of the page in English. And it's in the end of the second half, Salko Hrnjic and Mehmedovic Mehmed [as interpreted] are the names mentioned. In fact, Salka Hrnjic in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it is Muhamed Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mehmedovic Muhamed, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the four men that he didn't see die. He says: "At Snagovo, I saw four corpses also in the stage of decomposition, unrecognizable. These four who died at Krizevacke Njive I don't know personally, but I knew the two dead at Snagovo." And he says it is Salko Hrnjic and Muhamed Mehmedovic. He says both of them were from Kamenica. He says he heard from another person and discussed it with that other person. He says: "Concerning these two, Almir, known as Dzin, told me they had gotten killed in one of their earlier attempts to cross." We see the two men, although it's told by only one of them, who speak about the death of these two. Now, in the work of the institute, would it be a sufficient indication to proceed with investigation and establish that these two men had gotten killed during the attempt to break through? Were there fighting operations in Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be an important indication for us for further search. And as we said earlier, there was fighting at Snagovo and there were losses in that fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked about Kamenica at some point. Was there fighting at Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heavy fighting, yes. If I can just add one more thing. It says here both of them were from Kamenica. We don't know exactly which Kamenica he means, because we have Kamenica in the Bratunac municipality and one in the Zvornik municipality. Although for this purpose, it doesn't really matter. In both of them, there was fighting; but in Bratunac municipality in Kamenica, there were many more fatalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer is this document into evidence, Your Honour. The Prosecution's number since it has English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That it should be -- I think the English translation is not at this moment attached to the -- to 65 ter number -- oh, in this version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To this one it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be, Your Honour, D01400.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Any need to have it -- it is a public document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is public document, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the remainder of your re-examination, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber has some concerns on whether you really missed the point which was raised in chief. The point raised in chief was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I led chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In cross-examination, yes. In cross-examination. The issue was that there was a claim by this expert that he relied for his list on statements of persons who eye-witnessed someone to die, not whether finally where they died, how they died, et cetera, but it's the claim of that witness. You have not addressed that issue and that was, as far as -- and I checked with my colleagues - was the main and core issue dealt with in cross-examination. So, therefore, that is apparently then unaffected. But I leave it to you because you introduced the matter in a way where the Chamber had difficulties in understanding exactly whether you had got the core of what was the -- were the questions in cross-examination on this specific issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our position is that that test is too high and that -- not the test that the Prosecution followed so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's not a matter of -- and again you show that you may have missed the real point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I understand your point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The real point is that this witness claims that he relies on something, right or wrong, in whatever conclusions you want to draw, and that in cross-examination it was tested whether his sources really were about eye-witnesses, and whether he had good other reasons to draw some conclusions is a totally different matter. I leave it to this at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then you were asked about the statements of Seval Ademovic which in this case is 1D06227.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see it on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I think the reference my friend is looking for is 1D06277.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only a small passage from the end of this statement was put to you, but this is a longish statement. And we see on page 1 that this gentleman talks about the breakthrough towards Tuzla, and he obviously participated in it. I'd like to show you the second paragraph. It says: "I stress that from the very start of our breakthrough towards Tuzla, I didn't see my Jusuf again, but then during the exchange I found out that he had been killed in the area of Vlasenica." Then he talks about how they wandered about in the direction of Kuslat and Snagovo, how they tried to cross over the asphalt road towards Snagovo. After two or three days of wandering about, they are trying to reach Snagovo and then Memici --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I think we need the next page in English, just to let my friend know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, it's not there. I'm sorry. Can we move to another page in English, please. It's on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I can follow it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He says they came across the bodies of their own fighters who had got killed in trying to break out earlier and there were many wounded as well. And then he goes on to describe how they proceeded for the next five or six days, trying to reach Memici. And then comes the passage on the last page at the end, and you stressed in which way these statements are given, he mentions that: "In the breakout towards Tuzla, the following people got killed," and he gives the names. Did you understand then that he had direct knowledge about the death of the men mentioned in the last passage of this statement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I think his son got killed at Ruzina Voda as he was told, and I believe that he was from that locality. And, second, in the Serbian language when you say that somebody got killed in the context of the breakthrough, it means they got killed during fighting. If somebody was executed, the word "executed" would be used. But in the context in which he gives this statement to a security organ, he is talking about the knowledge that he has. If it was hearsay, he would have said: I was told that these people had got killed. So this leads to the conclusion that he was an eye-witness, although he doesn't explicitly say that. So it's an inference on my part. But in the context of everything he said and considering that he was giving this statement to a security organ, one can understand that he had seen them die.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look briefly again at the table that we uploaded in the system, D01399, or the old table, as my colleague referred to it earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting. That's not to be broadcast, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not to be broadcast. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to mention the name of the person. I'll just tell you in which line it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it, may I remind the parties that the new list is -- is neither tendered nor marked for identification. I don't know whether for a better understanding of the testimony of the witness that it would be good to have it in evidence, and I take it a translation might take less time than usual because most of the text is identical. I just remind you of that. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: I mentioned it this morning. I believe it was --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about the electronics in the Defence room.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came here for these two days on the 4th and 5th for preparation everything was blocked. There was a virus in your computers. So I had to work over the weekend in complete chaos.
