utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were representatives of the Tribunal involved in trying to solve the problem with the virus?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it goes. Probably somebody from the service came to deal with it. I don't know whether it was from the Defence or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to clear this up because I don't think it received proper attention. In this document, on page 2 - we can't broadcast it - in English, it's the last name that was discussed, and in B/C/S, it's fifth from the top. I'm interested in these numbers. You see CR12-161. Where did you find these numbers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the ICMP table from 2013. And it's possible I compared it with some other data, including maybe Mr. Sekic's [phoen] book about mass graves in Srebrenica that in its turn was based on information from the institute for missing persons, and information from Mr. Masovic whom I mentioned when I was last here in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In practice, because we have two numbers here, do you know who provided one and who provided the other? Was it the investigating authorities or the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from the authorities in the localities where exhumations are done, the pathologist has to do that and the laboratory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So somebody outside of the ICMP provided these numbers. Are they then able to know how these numbers are assigned to different parts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They shouldn't be able to know, and they know because when DNA analysis is done, it's a blind system in order to be objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll come later to these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's now time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today's examination prolonged a bit, but I will finish in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would you please -- the Chamber understood the main aspect of cross-examination to be methodological things, I rely on this, is it there, is it not there. That's rather more than -- at least I didn't hear much that individual conclusions, apart from the ones we dealt with, that that may be right, that may be wrong, but it's rather a -- it's rather a methodological criticism to the work done by the expert, including that he could overview only very -- a limited part of the available evidence and drew his conclusions on that. So if you would focus on what was the gist of the cross-examination, then we might move on most expeditiously. We take a break, and we resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We wait for the witness to enter the courtroom. It seems that Mr. Mladic is trying to draw the attention of counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we continue, Mr. Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see P07789 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked something about this document. This is a report on reassociation following re-exhumation of mortal remains. It is one of the persons that the Prosecutor asked you about. We've looked at the person in your list. The same numbers are mentioned. Two numbers. One is CR. That's the Cancari Road; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The other one is TIS. What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tisova Kosa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Even though this document was drawn up on the 4th of December, 2012, as it says here, it was disclosed to the Defence on the 21st of January, 2016, so that you could not see it. I will ask you anyway. Did the Defence ask you to deal with forensic evidence and check their accuracy while preparing your report? And are you a forensic expert?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that was not requested from me. And as you know, I'm not a forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your work at the institute for the missing persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you ask the ICMP to inform you about such mistakes as this one which occurred in the work of ICMP, according to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did they inform you about such mistakes, even if you didn't ask them to do it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know and to the best of my recollection, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a summary overview compiled by the ICMP that would present such mistakes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now move to 65 ter -- or, rather, it has a new number now, P07791.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is a document from the ICMP in which they explain what, in their view, happened. A part of the mandible is discussed. It was given this other label, the TIS label. The explanation does not include any precise information as to how this happened. The penultimate paragraph only says that it is possible that this bodily remain was wrongly stored, but it's not explained how that could have happened. The document was drawn up on the 27th of January, 2016.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just my friend said that one of the paragraphs here only says that it is possible that this bodily remain was wrongly stored, but -- oh no. My apologies, Your Honour. I thought my friend was talking about the reassociation itself. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] The document was written on last Wednesday. And just for the record, it's obvious that the Prosecution did some preparations and some verifications during the break in Mr. Pavlovic's testimony, so we would ask to be shown what was requested from the Bosnian authorities and who submitted information to them, and was this all that the Prosecution requested from the Bosnian authorities. As disclosure was really late, we would like to see what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you examining the witness at this moment or are you raising a matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I'm just putting that on the record. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, any problems in closing what has been asked and -- Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we can get together with them. They have been disclosed quite a bit of this material so they could see where this all came from. And there's nothing late about any of this given that, as you know, this material came the Sunday before the Monday of the testimony. But we've given them most everything we have, but we'll continue to explore what else they think there may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. Lukic touches upon a more general issue; that is, is there any record of recognised mistakes or errors in the ICMP conclusions? That's, Mr. Lukic, what I thought you were trying to elucidate in your examination. I take it that there's not because if there would be, that would be exculpatory evidence anyhow where there's an obligation to disclose that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's a rather broad topic, and as you know, there has been many updates of ICMP material correcting mistakes. The Skorpions being the most obvious. We have made an effort to keep up with that as much as we can, and again, we'll keep our eye out and see if there's anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And all that is disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. As far as we know, it's all been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would narrow down my request. It is something asked after Mr. Pavlovic left in relation to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Mr. McCloskey had answered that question already when I then broadened it a bit, and -- because he said he is willing to sit together with you and give information about whatever you've asked and what -- how it was prepared, Mr. McCloskey, if that's well understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's no problem. He has quite a bit of material right now, and if there's something in there that leads him to something else we'll absolutely get together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there will be full transparency by Mr. McCloskey if you sit together on what communications have taken place and what the results of all that has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I narrow it down to one matter. At the beginning of this letter from Mr. Parsons, ICMP, he refers to a letter or a recent inquiry concerning DNA-based reassociations. Was that a letter sent to ICMP, or was it another way of communication?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My memory was - and Mr. Lukic has this - it started off with an e-mail saying something to the effect of "can you check this out," and they wrote us back, and then we wrote a letter asking for a request. He has got all that material, and if he'd like to -- or if the Court would like it, we have it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I just wanted to know the background of this specific letter, but I think Mr. Lukic will be able to check if it is in his possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic raised his eyebrows when Mr. McCloskey said that he had received all of that. So, therefore, perhaps sitting together, coffee or tea, would assist in establishing that there indeed is full transparency and that's the only concern the Chamber would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would call the next document. It's 65 ter number 33617, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a death certificate --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this be broadcasted? I'm not sure, can you see the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This name has been checked with ICMP and it's fine to be broadcast, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see the name. It's Husein Alic, and you discuss this, the fact that it's a gun-shot/blast injury to the head. And on transcript page 42947, you said that you understood this as both injuries at once, a gun-shot and a blast injury. You also explained later on that a gun-shot wound doesn't exclude the possibility that someone may have perished during the breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before I continue, I would just offer this document into evidence since my learned friend did not do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then we need an English translation, so you would like to have it marked for identification --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then it could be MFI'd, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because I don't know, because I think we -- could we have a look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the second page what was discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could I have a look at that second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: If I may just -- thanks to my colleague Ms. Stewart, I can tell the Court we have requested an English translation for this and we should have it in a day or two. Just to clear up that matter [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. So it can be marked for identification. Let's start with that. Madam Registrar, the number under which it would be marked for identification -- oh, you want to tender it, Mr. -- or would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I have no objection to my friend tendering. It's just to let Mr. Lukic know he doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lukic tendered it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: -- have to ask for an English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the number -- the D number to be assigned would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, D01401 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is marked for identification pending translation. Because one of the things that struck me is that the whole emphasis was on whether it was a bullet wound or an explosive. But, of course, first of all, we need a translation not from B/C/S but from Latin. Because the medical expression starts with "destructio capitis." Now, I'm not that fluent in Latin anymore - I never was, as a matter of fact - but that sounds to me as that the head was destroyed, which, of course, then is also a relevant issue. I draw the attention of the parties to it, that they focused exclusively on part of what is written there in Latin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I see that there is B/C/S translation. I don't know whether -- that's a medical translation. But I don't know, Mr. Lukic, if you could read that slowly, then we could ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can do that much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gun-shot/blast destruction of the head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that there's -- so my knowledge of the Latin is still sufficient to resolve simple problems. But the destruction of the head, of course, has not been paid a lot of attention to. And let's move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, yesterday and earlier too, you talked about the number of missing persons and those who were killed during the events around Srebrenica. Do you know what is the total number of the casualties in the events in and around Srebrenica and the breakthrough of the column?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot precisely tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I understand that Mr. Lukic is trying to reference a part of Mr. Pavlovic's analysis which Your Honours explicitly was said outside of his competence. That is his conclusion on the number of people who died in the breakthrough in the column. That's how I understood Mr. Lukic to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. My question was total number of killed, missing, died in combat, total number in connection with Srebrenica from July 12th until the end of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that requires a knowledge, a thorough knowledge of who died in combat and who did not die in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, the total number of -- his institute worked with which number as casualties in regard of Srebrenica in July 1995. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All, whether executed, died in combat --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The whole -- the total number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The total number of those who --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic, just before anything is said, I just want to get clarification. You are saying at line 25 of page 51: "No, my question was total number of killed, died, missing, total number of ..." And then you say later: "No, the total number of -- his institute worked with which number as casualties in regard to Srebrenica ..." So you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All categories, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was another little problem for the Chamber that this has not been dealt with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I can make three quick points. Firstly, Mr. Lukic at the end of original question said "around the breakthrough of the column." That's why I stood up to object initially. Secondly, Your Honours, this is does not arise from cross. And, thirdly, Mr. Pavlovic has been very clear that he did not deal with mass executions. He doesn't know the evidence about it, he doesn't know the graves about it. So I think Mr. Lukic is asking him something he said he doesn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He didn't deal with the specific cases but he was -- I mean, in his work here, but I -- working for the institute of missing persons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- he did deal with the investigations even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're broadening now the scope of questions. We are now going beyond what the witness emphasised again and again, matters which he did not deal with in his report. That's one. Where he did not study lots of materials that were put to him, he again said, I only looked at testimony -- only at -- looked at statements given to those and those and those, and I only focused on what happened here. Therefore, the Chamber is not assisted by hearing this from this witness unless you -- but then it still would not be covered by cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was some kind of introduction, Your Honour. I don't -- because there was a challenge here and we did not have investigation in this case or in any other case in front of this Tribunal how many people died in -- in combat [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then to raise that issue after --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In combat -- we don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in examination-in-chief, then you should have presented that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was challenged here also by the Prosecution. Losses in combat. So I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Total numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Anything. There is nothing -- there is no investigation on that issue. We are working with our hands tied behind back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I still don't completely -- I still get confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask: Do you know how many -- what's the number of losses in combat of that column? No, you don't. Nobody does. Because nobody dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think, as a matter of fact, that the main issue is that the Prosecution has charged that people were killed and has given quite some details, and I don't know whether the Prosecution makes it a point on how many people exactly would have died in combat situations, whether that's relevant for their case. If it is not, but if it is relevant for you, Mr. Lukic, then you should have presented evidence on that, and not in questioning a witness in re-examination but to present it immediately. Mr. McCloskey, the Prosecution's position as far as overall number of persons who died in the, if I could say so, Srebrenica context, is that something which is part and a direct problem for you -- a direct issue in your case, apart from those you claim that have been killed, executed, as a part of a genocide?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that -- I can say it's an indirect part of our case. And there is quite a bit of evidence on that, and I could outline it very clearly. Mr. Lukic is not correct. It's probably -- and I would like to be able to now that he made this challenge, but of course it shouldn't be in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I could do it in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, a minute on the watch or a minute in your mind? Which is not always the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: A minute under the rules of Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's even worse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the matter. First of all, Mr. Lukic, you go really beyond the scope of cross-examination. Nevertheless, you raised the issue. We would not necessarily prohibit you from putting questions which are touching upon the issue, but it's really -- it's -- it's not the -- it has not been the subject matter of cross-examination. And in order to assist you in staying well within the lines, that is, you should stay within the scope of cross-examination, otherwise you would have had to present witnesses who deal with the matter, we give Mr. McCloskey an opportunity, three clock minutes, so that you are assisted better in phrasing your next questions, and we'll do that in the absence of the witness. Mr. Pavlovic, you're invited to wait for three minutes - well, perhaps four - outside this courtroom so that the parties can exchange views in preparation for the remainder of your examination. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, it is at this moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to say something to -- about the question. Mr. Lukic, before Mr. McCloskey speaks, can you please clearly state your question. You have said you wanted the total number of overall -- all categories of people who died.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And now you later said people who died in combat. What do you want? Do you want the overall people or do you want people who died in combat?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Overall. Overall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the question, overall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Mr. McCloskey offered us to -- offered to give the answer on that [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's listen to -- let's listen to Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're now -- I was about to tell Mr. McCloskey that it's now 13 minutes to 1.00 and that he has three minutes to explain what he wanted to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. I can -- as I think everyone knows, we have not charged particular crimes against the column except in the few incidences where we have survivors that have seen people captured in the column and executed, as we've heard here, and there's several of those incidences. And regarding the total number of people killed in the -- as the column left, I can refer you to the testimony, I believe, of Dean Manning and Dusan Janc, especially the report of Dusan Janc, who has collected all the information of the various NGOs and international communities that have gone through those woods and pulled out the surface remains. And it's many hundreds, I believe it's 6-, 7-, 800, I don't have the answer up-to-date. Can I say that how many more may be in those woods or not, we haven't attempted to say that. But we have attempted to give you all the evidence of all the human remains that have been found in those woods. That is Dusan Janc's report. And then, of course, given you the total number of missing that were reported missing by their families. Some over 75-, 7700, something like that. The total people coming out of mass graves, which is over 6.000, and then some 700, 800 people in the woods and their remains. This is fundamentally what the evidence gives you so you can get a total picture. He is completely wrong in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please, we will ask the witness to enter the courtroom again. Please be very clear in your questions and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just short response --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And again it was not a matter raised in cross-examination, so we'll be very precise on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But obviously the challenge is that we don't have answer how many of those killed in combat were buried in the same grave -- mass graves --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all nice, Mr. Lukic. You presented an expert witness with clear limitation in what he focused on, yes or no. You are bound by that and certainly not in re-examination to open another box which was neither opened by you in examination-in-chief nor was it in re-examination. And re-examination is not really a place to enter this -- to introduce this matter on which Mr. McCloskey said quite some evidence has been presented and witnesses could have been cross-examined on that matter by the Defence. Within these limitations, we'll allow you to put questions to the witness who is now expected to re-enter the courtroom. So could he be escorted in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, stay clearly within the boundaries I set out before and continue with your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And can I repeat this question on numbers or I move on? Total number or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to ask the witness what is the total number of -- if that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because the witness -- it is also not within his expertise and it is not in his report, it's not in cross-examination, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I accept that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the work of the institute, is there one list or there are separate lists for the victims of the breakthrough of the column and the victims of executions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only one list of missing persons where everybody should be included, both those who got killed during the breakthrough, in captivity, or otherwise. All the people who are registered as having gone missing in that area in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the work of the institute, or perhaps later, did you find out, apart from the victims of the Skorpion unit, whether any corpses of victims were found from the breakthrough of the column in any other area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or were they all buried in that area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a legal obligation at the institute to establish the circumstances of death and the causes of death. And according to what I know and what I said here, some were collected from the surface, and as for the rest, my assumption is that they had to be buried in the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly look at one more document. We are nearing the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On today's LiveNote, page 23, lines 21 through 24, it was put to you that roads in the area of Zvornik were not cleared up but only in the area of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we see D01397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're misstating what was put to the witness, Mr. Lukic. What was put to the witness is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can read it. So page 23, line 21, the question was: "So all you are aware of, then, in terms of evidence, is there was some clearing up of the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. That's all that's in your report. That's correct, isn't it?" Answer was: "If that's all I mentioned, then that's it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's about evidence stated in the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not what may have happened on the ground in either Zvornik or elsewhere --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is document from the report. It is. D01397.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then the witness apparently had forgotten about some materials, but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He said: If that's all what I mentioned. If that's all what I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. But that's a different matter than you earlier said was put to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have before us a document. We see at the top to whom it was sent. It's 20th July 1995. Among other people, it was sent to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade and also to the 1st Bratunac Infantry Brigade, and so on and so forth. It says: "Pursuant to the order of the Main Staff of the VRS dated 20th July 1995, and with the aim of locating and collecting human bodies and animal carcasses in the zones of responsibility of the units and burying them (internment cremation), and of removing, particularly in the areas of Srebrenica and Zepa and also Kamenica and Snagovo, everything that," et cetera. You mentioned today that there were two towns or villages of Kamenica, one in Bratunac municipality, another one in Zvornik municipality. Where is Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the area of Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It goes on: "I hereby order: "1. In co-operation with the civil defence organs, health centres and hospitals, enterprises and organisations, proceed with complete sanitization of the battlefield in your zone of responsibility, focusing on the Srebrenica and Zepa areas and roads leading from these areas towards Central Bosnia." What do you understand "towards Central Bosnia" to mean? Which axis is supposed to be sanitized?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Tuzla and Kladanj. That's precisely the direction in which the column was trying to break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Apart from the Bratunac municipality, would that cover other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. The Zvornik municipality and some others. Because this order designates a large number of units of the Drina Corps, as I understand all of these units belonged to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, thank you once again. This is all that the Defence has for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. MacDonald, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Just a couple, Your Honours. Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, just dealing with that last topic Mr. Lukic showed you as one of the orders you quote in your report there should be clearing up of the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Now, if we have the witness's report on the screen, please. It's D01373, page 30 in the English, page 27 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: You will see a paragraph number 1. Just above that, the sentence above that actually begins: "It is interesting to note that the author of this analysis was not able to find the reports of these units on the clearing up ..." So, Mr. Pavlovic, that order Mr. Lukic just read out to you, you found no reports indicating any clearing up had taken place. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I explain below --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, you answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacDonald. Mr. Pavlovic, this concludes your evidence in this court. We'd like to thank you very much for coming, not only once but even twice, and for having answered the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pavlovic just left, and we have some documents we proposed into evidence and the Prosecution maybe should address them. Or if it is too early --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It appears that Mr. Lukic has some expectations as far as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't quite catch the implication there, Your Honours. The Prosecution will tender the new list of Mr. Pavlovic seeing as we uploaded it, Your Honours. It's 65 ter 33644.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there's no translation yet --

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- therefore it should be marked for identification. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution P07792 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that's all I had, so I have to sit with Mr. McCloskey --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I leave it whether you want tea or coffee --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but you come back with a full transparency in communications following the testimony of the witness in December. I have one agenda item which I'd like to deal with at this moment, and that is about scheduling of the remainder of the case. During last week, the week of the 25th of January, Chamber staff met with the parties to discuss scheduling of the remainder of the Defence case. It emerged from that discussion that there were nine Defence witnesses left, not counting witness Dusan Pavlovic, who has just concluded his testimony. We'll move into private session to read out the name of these witnesses. Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Last week, the Chamber decided to hear evidence from one of the nine witnesses this week and urged the parties to do what is necessary to hear as many of the remaining eight witnesses during the first two weeks of March, that is the week of the 29th of February and the week of the 7th of March. The court sessions for the second, third, and fourth week of February are cancelled. And this was communicated to the parties and the Registry on the 26th of January and is hereby put on the record. The Chamber also understands the information provided by the Defence to mean that it intends to withdraw all remaining 92 ter motions related to witnesses who are not included in this final list. And could that be confirmed by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we get till the end of the day, Your Honour, for that, please? Probably yes, but I have to check with Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll -- if you could provide that information by --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- all those nine. I know. But I have to check with Mr. Ivetic. He is more privy with this issue at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we will wait until later today to receive this confirmation. I think that it's best to take the break now so that you call your next witness after the break. We'll take the break and we'll resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the next witness -- Mr. Tieger, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Before we bring the witness in, I have one matter to raise in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom for a while. And I would like to put another thing on the record already. Immediately before the break, we dealt with scheduling and not hearing evidence until the -- the week of the 29th of February. Of course, there was something scheduled, a court hearing which is not hearing evidence of a witness, and that is unaffected by what I said about scheduling. That we'll hear other matters, that's clear, I take it, to everyone. Does that deal with the matter, Mr. -- not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this is an opportunity, Mr. President, to rectify an earlier mistake in not introducing to the Court a member of the Prosecution team who has been in court with us earlier, and that is Mr. Rafael La Cruz, who I think was not formally introduced to the Court and should obviously have been, so we do so now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Welcome to the courtroom, Mr. La Cruz. If that's all, then we could ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. That would be Mr. Matijevic. And you'll examine him, Mr. Stojanovic, if I understand well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Matijevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Would you please make that declaration of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry that you waited so long because of our yesterday's estimate. Now, would you please tell us your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Mile Matijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, have you given a written statement to the Defence team of General Mladic answering the questions we put to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to call up in e-court 65 ter 1D05452.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, you will shortly see on the screen before you a text. If you can now see it on the right-hand side of the screen, is this personal -- are these personal details yours? And whose is the signature?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: The details I see in front of me are my details, and the signature is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, the signature we see on this page, is it yours?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like us to focus on paragraph 3 of this statement in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, yesterday when we were making the last preparations for your appearance in the courtroom, did you tell me that just for the sake of full precision, in the first word of paragraph 3, instead of "there," we should change to "at the centre of the security services, I was first assigned," et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Matijevic, having clarified this in paragraph 3 and upon making a solemn declaration here in the courtroom and having reviewed your statement once again yesterday, if we were to put to you the same questions again, would you give the same answers as in the text in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would give identical answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be to the best of your recollection on the circumstances you described?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this witness's statement, 65 ter 1D05452, with the proviso that in e-court, as I have discussed with my learned friend from the Prosecution, a duplicate of this statement should be deleted from e-court. Because we had uploaded another version intending to tender it under 92 bis. I hereby tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D01402, public.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just so I understand the technical side -- we have no objections to the admission of one statement through the witness. Just so I understand the technical side, will it be, once it's marked for identification, possible for the Defence to correct the upload or is Mr. Stojanovic asking that the Registry be requested to remove one of the two versions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We discussed this before the beginning. I'm not sure whether our case manager would technically be able to do it. If she's able to do it, she will; but if that's not possible, then we would ask assistance from the Registry to remove the earlier version from the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, whether it needs to be removed from the system, yes or no, what we see at this moment on our screen is apparently the document as uploaded by the Defence which the Defence seeks to be admitted. Any further comments? Because what else is in the system as long as it's not tendered or if it is part of a withdrawn motion, that's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the reason and I think what Mr. Stojanovic was pointing to was both versions and there's only one -- there aren't significant differences but both versions are uploaded under the same 65 ter number. So if 65 ter 1D05452 is admitted, then everything under that number, as I understand it, gets admitted, both versions, and so we're just talking about how to technically remove the duplicate from that single number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- Madam Registrar, does this cause any problem if we would now decide to have the document as it is on our screen as called up by Mr. Stojanovic, to have it admitted into evidence, or do we get for free another copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can admit it into evidence upon the confirmation of Madam Registrar that it causes no problems. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I said admitted into evidence but I may have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, there's no number -- it has a number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I must have been unclear when I said admitted into evidence earlier. But let's now make it ... one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is D1402, which is hereby admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the Court. With your leave, I should like to read the short summary of Mr. Matijevic's statement. Witness Mile Matijevic has a Ph.D. in law and works as a professor in Banja Luka. He spent his professional career in a variety of duties at the republic Secretariat for Internal Affairs of Serbia, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and finally Republika Srpska. From the establishment of the MUP of Republika Srpska, he worked at the Security Services Centre of Banja Luka. And beginning with mid-1994, he worked at the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska in Bijeljina. And from 1995 onwards, he dedicated himself to education and the training of MUP staff in Republika Srpska. In his statement, he describes his career in detail. While he was living and working at the CSB Banja Luka, in the course of his duties and by the nature of his job, he had direct co-operation with military authorities, especially the security organs of the 1st and the 2nd Krajina Corps. He also describes in detail the system of control and command at the then-CSB Banja Luka. He also talks about his impressions about the operation and work of the public security centre Prijedor, as well as the work style of the then-chief of this SJB, Simo Drljaca, who was wont to make decisions bypassing the prior and necessary consultations with CSB Banja Luka. There were also situations when he didn't even inform the CSB about certain events in the territory of the SJB Prijedor. In connection with references to his name in the diary entries of General Mladic in the text of the 27th May 1993, he stresses that he is personally unaware of any meeting comprised of the people listed in these notes. He is unaware that such a meeting was ever held. He never attended any meeting in the said composition of persons, nor does he know what Colonel Bogojevic reported to General Mladic. He was very surprised to find his name in the context of the said meeting. Otherwise, he collaborated with Colonel Bogojevic on issues concerning the employment of police units in combat operations and on other forms of co-operation between military and police forces. This is, Your Honours, the short summary of Mr. Matijevic's statement. I have just a few questions for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, in your statement, you say that you had some form of co-operation with Colonel Bogojevic. To the best of your knowledge, what were the duties and responsibilities of Colonel Bogojevic in the period when you were in contact with him?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Working in the Security Services Centre and earlier in the police, my job was to liaise with the security organs of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps mainly concerning the use of police officers in combat operations. On this issue, we collaborated by agreeing on the number of personnel from the police needed by the military in certain localities at the request of the VRS. This colonel was doing his job and I did not need to be informed about all aspects of his job. I only knew the aspect concerning the resubordination of police members to the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Colonel Bogojevic hold this position of the security organ in the 1st Krajina Corps all the time of the war, or did you have to liaise with any other officers of that corps?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Bogojevic took over as chief of security from late Milan Stevilovic who got killed on the 5th of July, 1992, together with the chief of police, Stevan Markovic. They were ambushed in the area of Kotor Varos and both of them got killed. And after their death, I was appointed chief of the security at the CSB, and he became chief of security in the corps. So I knew Colonel Stevilovic before him, although I didn't have much contact with him, but later on I continued to collaborate with Colonel Bogojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record and for the Court, could you tell us if Colonel Bogojevic is still alive?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard recently that he died a couple of months ago. After the war I had no further contact with him. He was seriously ill, and as far as I know, he died from a stroke.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Matijevic, for these answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these were all the questions we had for Mr. Matijevic for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Matijevic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right, standing. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to talk briefly about the mechanics of your co-operation with the VRS. Now, did I understand correctly from your answers on direct examination that you would liaise directly personally with Colonel Bogojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I contacted him directly in certain situations when it was determined by my superiors that we should agree about certain operational engagement of members of police and army on the ground. And, likewise, I met him at the front because I spent quite some time with police members in the field and on the fronts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Would you just meet him at the front or also in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka, we would sit together occasionally as the need arose, whether in his office in the corps or on our premises in the police. It was not necessary very often. More often, we had telephone contacts or we sent dispatches, but sometimes we did meet and sit together, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you met, would you meet alone or would others attend?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I really don't remember details of specific meetings now. I think these were more often meetings where there were many of us, where we agreed about the engagement of members of the police at the request of the army or perhaps some other issues that had to do with our joint activities. But probably we sometimes sat alone, just the two of us, but I really cannot remember the details or specific instances right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say "other issues that had to do with our joint activities," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as part of our duties, the members of the police and military security, one question that was very topical were our measures taken against soldiers in case they violated regulations in public or if they deserted from their units and similar issues, where members of the police intervened and then we handed them over to the relevant military organs for further processing. So these were some of the issues that required us to have contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say you handed them over to military organs. That's because the military had exclusive jurisdiction over any violations by soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. We were authorised to react in the first instance, but our duty was then to transfer this to the jurisdiction of the military organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And would you say you had a good working relationship with Colonel Bogojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: During the time when we co-operated, and that was less than two years, there were no special problems. No problems with regard to our co-operation and our official duties. We carried out all our duties properly in accordance with the tasks that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the 2nd Krajina Corps -- Bogojevic was who you had contact with in the 1st Krajina Corps. Who was it in the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: In the 2nd Krajina Corps, the chief of security was Lieutenant-Colonel - later colonel - Mikajlo Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You would also communicate with him about common tasks?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, about the same issues that we discussed with our colleagues from the 1st Krajina Corps. Because the Security Services Centre was in charge of the zone of the 2nd Krajina Corps and one part of the zone of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did you have a good working relationship with Colonel Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And also with Colonel Bogojevic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, also with Bogojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33599.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm just going to look quickly at one example of a joint operation. This is a commendation sent to the MUP special unit and the MUP information minister and all SJBs in the region from Mr. Zupljanin, dated the 2nd of November, 1992. We see a reference to members of several police stations and those enrolled in a policemen's course in Banja Luka who had been among the first to enter Jajce, clearing it of the remnants of Ustasha-Muslim forces. And it refers to, a couple of lines lower, a "synchronized action with the army." And turning to page 2 in the English and page 1 at the bottom in the B/C/S, we see several people are commended by name, including you. Do you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what was your role in the Jajce operation?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: In the Jajce zone - I think that this was in late 1992 - a military action was carried out in the Jajce area. It was the liberation of Jajce. In co-ordinated action with military units were -- was a number of policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: As members of the police were in the composition of those units, somebody from the police had also to be in the staff of the units. Even though it was a military command, it was our obligation to be present there because our members were engaged. And, I'm sorry, I also see here, and it's true, that the special unit of the Republika Srpska MUP also participated in this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who had overall command of the Jajce operation?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No. No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry. I think there may have been a translation issue. What I asked you was who, what person, had overall command of the Jajce operation?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm sorry, I heard the question whether I was the commander. Even if I had wanted to, I couldn't have been the commander because it was the army that commanded. And to be frank, I don't remember for sure who it was. It was a big operation where one part of the corps participated. It must have been a high-ranking army officer at the level of the division or so. I was simply present there in the staff as the co-ordinator of liaison with the police, so I was in charge of logistics. Because the command was absolutely in the hands of the army, and the army was leading this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was standard during these joint operations, the top command would be the army; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to regulations, the army carried out combat operations and policemen participated in certain activities because they were not by themselves entitled to carry out combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 16975.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order from Mr. Zupljanin dated the 27th of October, 1992, a few days earlier. If we zoom in at the very top, he begins that: "Pursuant to a request from the command of the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS to engage 158 members of the police from the Banja Luka CSB region, who will be resubordinated to the 1st KK command to execute designated tasks in Jajce." And then he orders which stations will send which personnel. Now, the term used in the regulations for when the army has the top command, as you just described was standard, is resubordination; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mentioned the last one referred to the special unit. If we look below the list of what personnel will come from what SJB, we see a reference to Brane Pecanac commanding the unit of these 158 members of the police. That's the special unit that you saw referred to in the last document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we saw the previous document was dated the 2nd of November, 1992, the commendation. What you refer to as the liberation of Jajce happened at the beginning of November 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, late October and early November. I think it was roughly that period. I don't know exactly, I don't remember, but one can see from these dates that that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 33599 and 16975.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, those will be Exhibits P07793 and P07794, public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7793 and P7794 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to go into more detail about the Jajce operation, but the Chamber has received evidence coming from CSB Banja Luka - and I'm referring to P3216 and P3853 - that there were about 33.000 Muslims and Croats in Jajce before the war, 31.000 had moved out by 1993, and by 1995 there were barely 100. Now, you were aware that during and after what you call the liberation of Jajce, tens of thousands of Muslims and Croats had fled to Central Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: This specific situation in the Jajce area and further afield is something that I'm only generally aware of. I'm not a military strategist or a commander. But knowing the situation to a degree, it was such that in view of the multi-ethnic composition of the population of Jajce and the surrounding area, as early as -- at the beginning of the war, the conflict between armed forces, both Serb, Muslim and Croat ones, was very fierce, and it so happened that in certain areas, the Muslims left their territory; in other areas, it was the Serbs; and in the third, the Croats. And so on and so forth. So it was a situation that was typical of the municipalities in the Jajce zone and the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware, because you worked at the CSB when it collected this information, that Jajce was one of the areas that because of the destruction of their neighbourhoods, because of the crimes committed against them, the Muslims and Croats left; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I see we're close to the end of the day. I just have one more question for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33604.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a portion of your testimony in Bosnia in the Mejakic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 11 in the English and 12 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I'm a bit confused. You said it's "a portion of your testimony." It seems to be a statement given, if I look at the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's a transcript of the Court of BiH testimony. The format that we get those in looks like the format that we see OTP interviews in on the screen. But -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I understand better that -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm just going to read you one of the answers you gave there, beginning at line 12 in the B/C/S, and ask you if you stand by it as truthful and accurate. It's about the structure of the RS MUP. You testified: "MUP of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, later on - Serb Republic, is, in essence, one centralised and organised in hierarchy, in hierarchy order, that is the ... it is the body. So in a vertical structure, the MUP is organised in a way that it was dealt ... it was led by the minister of the MUP who is authorised towards all the lower bodies, directly or through his subordinates, through the organisational unit in the seat of the Ministry, and through organisational units that are situated in the field." Do you stand by that testimony today as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I see we're at the time to break for the afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are already beyond the time to break. Witness, before we adjourn for the day, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether that is testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that's clear to you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30, in this same courtroom. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 3rd of February, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of February, 2016, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
